Lutheranism.fact: Scripture alone is the formal principle of the faith, the final authority for all matters of faith and morals because of its inspiration, authority, clarity, efficacy, and sufficiency. The authority of the Scriptures has been challenged during the history of Lutheranism.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Theological conservatives use the historical-grammatical method of _____ interpretation, while theological liberals use the higher critical method
Lutheranism.fact: Theological conservatives use the historical-grammatical method of Biblical interpretation, while theological liberals use the higher critical method.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: The Apology of the _____ identifies Holy Scripture with the Word of God and calls the Holy Spirit the author of the Bible
Lutheranism.fact: The Apology of the Augsburg Confession identifies Holy Scripture with the Word of God and calls the Holy Spirit the author of the Bible.

Lutheranism.fact: Because of this, Lutherans confess in the Formula of Concord, "we receive and embrace with our whole heart the prophetic and apostolic Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments as the pure, clear fountain of Israel". Lutheranism.subject: Important Days

Lutheranism.fact: A correct translation of their writings is seen as God's Word because it has the same meaning as the original Hebrew and Greek.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: In addition, _____ believe that God's Word is freely accessible to every reader or hearer of ordinary intelligence, without requiring any special education
Lutheranism.fact: In addition, Lutherans believe that God's Word is freely accessible to every reader or hearer of ordinary intelligence, without requiring any special education. As a result of this, Lutherans do not believe there is a need to wait for any clergy, pope, scholar, or ecumenical council to explain the real meaning of any part of the Bible.

Lutheranism.question: A _____ must understand the language that scriptures are presented in, and should not be so preoccupied by error so as to prevent understanding
Lutheranism.fact: In addition, Lutherans believe that God's Word is freely accessible to every reader or hearer of ordinary intelligence, without requiring any special education. A Lutheran must understand the language that scriptures are presented in, and should not be so preoccupied by error so as to prevent understanding.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days

Lutheranism.fact: Holy Scripture is not a dead letter, but rather, the power of the Holy Spirit is inherent in it.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: As the _____ affirm, "in those things which concern the spoken, outward Word, we must firmly hold that God grants His Spirit or grace to no one, except through or with the preceding outward Word"
Lutheranism.fact: As the Smalcald Articles affirm, "in those things which concern the spoken, outward Word, we must firmly hold that God grants His Spirit or grace to no one, except through or with the preceding outward Word".

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: There are no deficiencies in _____ that need to be supplanted with tradition, pronouncements of the Pope, new revelations, or present-day development of doctrine
Lutheranism.fact: Holy Scripture is not a dead letter, but rather, the power of the Holy Spirit is inherent in it. Scripture does not compel a mere intellectual assent to its doctrine, resting on logical argumentation, but rather it creates the living agreement of faith.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Properly distinguishing between Law and _____ prevents the obscuring of the Gospel teaching of justification by grace through faith alone
Lutheranism.fact: Tradition is still a norm (norma normata)." Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: The doctrinal positions of _____ churches are not uniform because the Book of Concord does not hold the same position in all Lutheran churches
Lutheranism.fact: Tradition is still a norm (norma normata)." Lutheranism.fact: Furthermore, the Lutheran churches teach "Scripture as 'the norm which norms (but which is not itself normed)’ (norma normans or norma normans non normata) and Tradition, especially the ecumenical creeds, as ‘the norms which are normed’ (norma normata)." As such, Lutherans hold that "Although Scripture cannot be normed by Tradition (norma normans non normata), it can be, and is, interpreted through Tradition. Tradition is still a norm (norma normata)." In the Lutheran churches, tradition is r...

Lutheranism.fact: For example, the state churches in Scandinavia consider only the Augsburg Confession as a "summary of the faith" in addition to the three ecumenical creeds.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Lutheran pastors, congregations, and church bodies in _____ and the Americas usually agree to teach in harmony with the entire Lutheran confessions
Lutheranism.fact: Lutheran pastors, congregations, and church bodies in Germany and the Americas usually agree to teach in harmony with the entire Lutheran confessions.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days

Lutheranism.fact: Some Lutheran church bodies require this pledge to be unconditional because they believe the confessions correctly state what the Bible teaches. Others allow their congregations to do so "insofar as" the confessions are in agreement with the Bible.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days

Lutheranism.fact: In addition, Lutherans accept the teachings of the first seven ecumenical councils of the Christian Church. Lutherans traditionally see themselves as the "main trunk of the historical Christian Tree" set up by Christ and the Apostles, holding that during the Reformation, the Church of Rome fell away.

Lutheranism.fact: Lutherans traditionally see themselves as the "main trunk of the historical Christian Tree" set up by Christ and the Apostles, holding that during the Reformation, the Church of Rome fell away.

Lutheranism.fact: Lutherans believe that humans are saved from their sins by God's grace alone (Sola Gratia), through faith alone (Sola Fide), on the basis of Scripture alone (Sola Scriptura).

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: However, _____ and Eve chose to disobey God, trusting in their own strength, knowledge, and wisdom
Lutheranism.fact: However, Adam and Eve chose to disobey God, trusting in their own strength, knowledge, and wisdom.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: For many _____, original sin is the "chief sin, a root and fountainhead of all actual sins"
Lutheranism.fact: For many Lutherans, original sin is the "chief sin, a root and fountainhead of all actual sins". Lutherans teach that sinners, while capable of doing works that are outwardly "good", are not capable of doing works that satisfy God's justice.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: God in eternity has turned _____ heart to this world and planned for its redemption because he loves all people and does not want anyone to be eternally damned
Lutheranism.fact: God in eternity has turned His Fatherly heart to this world and planned for its redemption because he loves all people and does not want anyone to be eternally damned.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Saving faith is the knowledge of, acceptance of, and trust in the promise of the _____
Lutheranism.fact: Saving faith is the knowledge of, acceptance of, and trust in the promise of the Gospel.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Even faith itself is seen as a gift of God, created in the hearts of _____ by the work of the Holy Spirit through the Word and Baptism
Lutheranism.fact: Even faith itself is seen as a gift of God, created in the hearts of Christians by the work of the Holy Spirit through the Word and Baptism.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Thus, _____ reject the "decision theology" which is common among modern evangelicals, including Baptists and Methodists
Lutheranism.fact: Thus, Lutherans reject the "decision theology" which is common among modern evangelicals, including Baptists and Methodists. To Lutherans, grace is not about our response to God's gifts, but only His gifts.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: The term "grace" has been defined differently by other _____ church bodies
Lutheranism.fact: Even faith itself is seen as a gift of God, created in the hearts of Christians by the work of the Holy Spirit through the Word and Baptism. The term "grace" has been defined differently by other Christian church bodies.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: For _____s, "good works are necessary fruits of faith in the life of a Christian and that they proceed from a renewed heart that is thankful to God for His mercy and love"

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: These good works done by _____ are rewarded by God
Lutheranism.fact: For Christians, "good works are necessary fruits of faith in the life of a Christian and that they proceed from a renewed heart that is thankful to God for His mercy and love". These good works done by Christians are rewarded by God.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Faith apprehends the grace of God in _____ whereby the person is justified
Lutheranism.fact: For Christians, "good works are necessary fruits of faith in the life of a Christian and that they proceed from a renewed heart that is thankful to God for His mercy and love". These good works done by Christians are rewarded by God.

Lutheranism.fact: Thus good works always follow justifying faith and are certainly to be found with it, since such faith is never alone but is always accompanied by love and hope." (FC, Epitome, Article III.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days

Lutheranism.fact: Lutheran theology holds that Christians freely and willingly serve God and their neighbors. The Lutheran churches teach that God rewards good works done by Christians, with "each one receiving his/her own reward according to his/her labour"; the Apology of the Augsburg Confession teaches: "We also affirm what we have often said, that although justification and eternal life go along with faith, nevertheless, good works merit other bodily and spiritual rewards and degrees of reward.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Lutherans believe the _____ proceeds from both the Father and the Son
Lutheranism.fact: Lutherans believe the Holy Spirit proceeds from both the Father and the Son.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: In the words of the _____: "We worship one God in Trinity, and Trinity in Unity; Neither confounding the Persons, nor dividing the Substance
Lutheranism.fact: In the words of the Athanasian Creed: "We worship one God in Trinity, and Trinity in Unity; Neither confounding the Persons, nor dividing the Substance.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days

Lutheranism.fact: In the words of the Athanasian Creed: "We worship one God in Trinity, and Trinity in Unity; Neither confounding the Persons, nor dividing the Substance. For there is one Person of the Father, another of the Son, and another of the Holy Ghost.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: The doctrines of the perpetual virginity of Mary and _____ of Mary are maintained as pious opinions by many Lutherans, both being held by Martin Luther himself
Lutheranism.fact: The doctrines of the perpetual virginity of Mary and Sinlessness of Mary are maintained as pious opinions by many Lutherans, both being held by Martin Luther himself.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: A number of historic _____ churches have a Lady chapel dedicated to the Blessed Virgin Mary
Lutheranism.fact: The doctrines of the perpetual virginity of Mary and Sinlessness of Mary are maintained as pious opinions by many Lutherans, both being held by Martin Luther himself. A number of historic Lutheran churches have a Lady chapel dedicated to the Blessed Virgin Mary.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: The definition of sacrament in the Apology of the _____ lists Absolution as one of them
Lutheranism.fact: The definition of sacrament in the Apology of the Augsburg Confession lists Absolution as one of them.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Private Confession is expected before receiving the _____ for the first time
Lutheranism.fact: Lutherans are not dogmatic about the number of the sacraments, though three sacraments are generally recognized: baptism, confession, and the eucharist. Private Confession is expected before receiving the Eucharist for the first time.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Some churches also allow for individual absolution on _____ before the Eucharistic service
Lutheranism.fact: Some churches also allow for individual absolution on Saturdays before the Eucharistic service.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: A _____ and Absolution, known as the Penitential Rite, is proclaimed in the Eucharistic liturgy
Lutheranism.fact: A General Confession and Absolution, called the Penitential Rite, is proclaimed in the Eucharistic liturgy.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Even though baptized infants cannot articulate that faith, _____ believe that it is present all the same
Lutheranism.fact: Even though baptized infants cannot articulate that faith, Lutherans believe that it is present all the same. It is faith alone that receives these divine gifts, so Lutherans confess that baptism "works forgiveness of sins, delivers from death and the devil, and gives eternal salvation to all who believe this, as the words and promises of God declare".

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: In the special section on infant baptism in his _____, Luther argues that infant baptism is God-pleasing because persons so baptized were reborn and sanctified by the Holy Spirit
Lutheranism.fact: In the special section on infant baptism in his Large Catechism, Luther argues that infant baptism is God-pleasing because persons so baptized were reborn and sanctified by the Holy Spirit.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Lutherans affirm that the _____ of the Mass (sacrificium eucharistikon) is a sacrifice of thanksgiving and praise (sacrificia laudis)
Lutheranism.fact: Lutherans affirm that the Sacrifice of the Mass (sacrificium eucharistikon) is a sacrifice of thanksgiving and praise (sacrificia laudis).

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: The Eucharist is celebrated as the central part of the Mass (_____), especially on the Lord's Day
Lutheranism.fact: The Eucharist is celebrated as the central part of the Mass (Divine Service), especially on the Lord's Day.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Lutherans may prepare for the reception of _____ by observing the Eucharistic Fast, which typically begins at midnight and concludes at the reception of the eucharistic elements
Lutheranism.fact: Lutherans may prepare for the reception of Holy Communion by observing the Eucharistic Fast, which typically begins at midnight and concludes at the reception of the eucharistic elements.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Partaking in the sacrament of confession and absolution is, according to the Book of _____, considered proper preparation for receiving the sacrament
Lutheranism.fact: Partaking in the sacrament of confession and absolution is, according to the Book of Concord, considered proper preparation for receiving the sacrament.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Prior to going to _____ and receiving Absolution, the faithful are expected to examine their lives in light of the Ten Commandments
Lutheranism.fact: Prior to going to Confessing and receiving Absolution, the faithful are expected to examine their lives in light of the Ten Commandments.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: An order of _____ and Absolution is contained in the Small Catechism, as well as in liturgical books
Lutheranism.fact: Partaking in the sacrament of confession and absolution is, according to the Book of Concord, considered proper preparation for receiving the sacrament. An order of Confession and Absolution is contained in the Small Catechism, as well as in liturgical books.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Clergy are prohibited from revealing anything said during private _____ and Absolution per the Seal of the Confessional, and face excommunication if it is violated
Lutheranism.fact: An order of Confession and Absolution is contained in the Small Catechism, as well as in liturgical books. Lutherans receive the sacrament of 'confession and absolution' in a confessional, reconciliation room, or by kneeling at the communion rail, to confess their sins, while the confessor listens and then offers absolution while laying their stole on the penitent's head.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Apart from this, _____ have a practice of lay confession
Lutheranism.fact: Apart from this, Laestadian Lutherans have a practice of lay confession.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Additional ordinances are observed by _____, such as feetwashing (especially on Maundy Thursday), as well as historically, head covering for Christian women during prayer and worship
Lutheranism.fact: Apart from this, Laestadian Lutherans have a practice of lay confession. Additional ordinances are observed by Lutherans, such as feetwashing (especially on Maundy Thursday), as well as historically, head covering for Christian women during prayer and worship.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Lutherans believe that although humans have free will concerning civil righteousness, they cannot work spiritual righteousness in the heart without the presence and aid of the _____
Lutheranism.fact: Lutherans believe that although humans have free will concerning civil righteousness, they cannot work spiritual righteousness in the heart without the presence and aid of the Holy Spirit.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: In Lutheran theology, "God desires the salvation of every single human being who has ever lived" and _____ died for the sins of all people
Lutheranism.fact: In Lutheran theology, "God desires the salvation of every single human being who has ever lived" and Jesus died for the sins of all people.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Lutherans believe that those who trust in _____, and manifest their living faith by serving God, can be certain of their salvation
Lutheranism.fact: Lutherans believe that those who trust in Christ, and manifest their living faith by serving God, can be certain of their salvation. According to Lutheranism, the central final hope of the Christian is "the resurrection of the body and the life everlasting" as confessed in the Apostles' Creed rather than predestination.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Lutherans disagree with those who make predestination—rather than _____'s suffering, death, and resurrection—the source of salvation
Lutheranism.fact: Lutherans believe that those who trust in Christ, and manifest their living faith by serving God, can be certain of their salvation. According to Lutheranism, the central final hope of the Christian is "the resurrection of the body and the life everlasting" as confessed in the Apostles' Creed rather than predestination.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Instead, _____ teach eternal damnation is a result of the unbeliever's sins, rejection of the forgiveness of sins, and unbelief
Lutheranism.fact: Lutherans disagree with those who make predestination—rather than Christ's suffering, death, and resurrection—the source of salvation. Unlike some Calvinists, Lutherans do not believe in a predestination to damnation, usually referencing "God our Savior, who desires all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth" as contrary evidence to such a claim.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: The explanation of the _____' Creed given in the Small Catechism declares that everything good that people have is given and preserved by God, either directly or through other people or things
Lutheranism.fact: The explanation of the Apostles' Creed given in the Small Catechism declares that everything good that people have is given and preserved by God, either directly or through other people or things.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Lutherans teach that, at death, the souls of _____ are immediately taken into the presence of Jesus, where they await the second coming of Jesus on the last day
Lutheranism.fact: Lutherans teach that, at death, the souls of Christians are immediately taken into the presence of Jesus, where they await the second coming of Jesus on the last day.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: After the resurrection of all the dead, and the change of those still living, all nations shall be gathered before _____, and he will separate the righteous from the wicked
Lutheranism.fact: After the resurrection of all the dead, and the change of those still living, all nations shall be gathered before Christ, and he will separate the righteous from the wicked. Christ will publicly judge all people by the testimony of their deeds, the good works of the righteous in evidence of their faith, and the evil works of the wicked in evidence of their unbelief.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Martin Luther was a great proponent of music, and this is why music forms a central part of _____ services to this day
Lutheranism.fact: Martin Luther was a great proponent of music, and this is why music forms a central part of Lutheran services to this day. Lutheran hymns are sometimes called chorales.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Johann Sebastian Bach, a devout _____, composed a huge body of sacred music for the Lutheran church
Lutheranism.fact: Lutheran hymns are sometimes called chorales. Lutheran hymnody is well known for its doctrinal, didactic, and musical richness.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Many Lutherans also preserve a liturgical approach to the celebration of the _____/Communion, emphasizing the Sacrament as the central act of Christian worship
Lutheranism.fact: Many Lutherans also preserve a liturgical approach to the celebration of the Holy Eucharist/Communion, emphasizing the Sacrament as the central act of Christian worship.

Lutheranism.subject: Important Days
Lutheranism.question: Lutherans believe that the actual body and blood of _____ are present in, with and under the bread and the wine

World Milk Day.fact: == History == World Milk Day was first designated by the FAO in 2001.  June 1 was chosen as the date because many countries were already celebrating a milk day during that time of year.  The Day provides an opportunity to focus attention on milk and raise awareness of dairy’s part in healthy diets, responsible food production, and supporting livelihoods and communities.  This is supported by FAO data showing that more than one billion people's livelihoods are supported by the dairy sector and that dairy is consumed by more than six billion people globally.  The fact that many countries choose to do this on the same day lends additional importance to individual national celebrations and shows that milk is a global food.  === World Milk Day celebrations === World Milk Day 2016 In 2016, World Milk Day was celebrated in over 40 countries.  Activities included marathons and family runs, milking demonstrations and farm visits, school-based activities, concerts, conferences and seminars, competitions and a range of events focusing on promoting the value of milk and illustrating the important role played by the dairy industry in the national economy

World Water Day.fact: World Water Day is an annual United Nations (UN) observance day held on 22 March that highlights the importance of fresh water.  The day is used to advocate for the sustainable management of freshwater resources.  The theme of each year focuses on topics relevant to clean water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), which is in line with the targets of Sustainable Development Goal 6.  The UN World Water Development Report (WWDR) is released each year around World Water Day.  UN-Water is the convener for World Water Day and selects the theme for each year in consultation with UN organizations that share an interest in that year's focus.  The theme for 2021 was "Valuing Water" and the public campaign invited people to join a global conversation on social media to "tell us your stories, thoughts and feelings about water"

In 2020, due to the COVID-19 pandemic, there was an additional focus on hand washing and hygiene.  Relevant issues include water scarcity, water pollution, inadequate water supply, lack of sanitation, and the impacts of climate change (which is the theme of World Water Day 2020).  The day brings to light the inequality of access to WASH services and the need to assure the human right to water and sanitation.  The World Water Day website announces events, activities and volunteer opportunities. UN-Water mobilizes organizations of all kinds to action, whether globally or locally.  == Examples of activities == Non-governmental organizations active in the WASH sector, such as UNICEF, WaterAid and Water and Sanitation for the Urban Poor (WSUP), use the day to raise public awareness and get media attention for water issues and inspire action. In reflection of this declaration, the 2013 World Water Day was dedicated to water cooperation.  === 2014 – Water and Energy === The 2014 theme of Water and Energy emphasized the close linkages and interdependence of water and energy and brought attention to the water-energy nexus.  About 8% of the energy generated globally is used for pumping, treating and transporting water to various consumers.
